ai.literal: Wealth lost even-when, old-ties cherishing kinsmen with-indeed are-found.
ai.translation: Even when one's wealth is lost, the cherishing of old ties is found only among kinsmen.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய செல்வம் அழிந்த காலத்திலும், பழைய உறவைப் பாராட்டி அன்பு செலுத்தும் பண்பு சுற்றத்தாரிடமே உள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the enduring nature of true kinship. The word 'paṟṟu' generally means attachment or hold, but in this context, it specifically refers to wealth or resources that one holds onto. Even when a person loses all their wealth and becomes destitute, it is only their true relatives who will remember their old ties ('paḻaimai') and continue to cherish them. The emphatic suffix 'ē' in 'kaṇṇē' stresses that this unconditional loyalty is an exclusive trait found only among one's kin.

ai.literal: Affection unceasing kin if-joins, budding unceasing prosperity many will-give.
ai.translation: If one secures kin whose affection never ceases, it will yield many forms of ever-budding prosperity.
ai.modern: அன்பு குறையாத சுற்றத்தார் ஒருவருக்கு அமைந்தால், அது அவருக்குத் தொடர்ந்து வளரும் பல செல்வங்களைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the value of maintaining close ties with loving relatives. The phrase 'viruppu aṟā' describes kin whose affection is never severed. When a person is surrounded by such people, it brings 'aruppu aṟā ākkam', meaning prosperity that never stops budding or growing. The imagery of a continuously budding plant illustrates how supportive relationships naturally and endlessly generate success and wealth.

ai.literal: Mingling he-who-is-without life, pond's-expanse bank without water having-filled like-that.
ai.translation: The life of one who does not mingle intimately with his kindred is like a vast pond filling with water without a bank to hold it.
ai.modern: சுற்றத்தாருடன் மனம் விட்டுப் பழகும் தன்மை இல்லாதவனின் வாழ்க்கையானது, கரையில்லாத ஒரு பெரிய குளத்தில் நீர் நிறைவதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the life of a person who lacks intimacy with their relatives to a vast pond that has no banks. Just as water flowing into a bankless pond simply runs off and is wasted without benefiting anyone, the wealth and life of someone who does not embrace their kindred will not be sustained or useful. The word 'அளவளா' refers to mingling freely and intimately, highlighting the emotional bond needed to hold a family together, much like a bank holds water.

ai.literal: By kin to be surrounded living, wealth indeed by the acquiring obtained fruit.
ai.translation: Living surrounded by one's kin is the true fruit gained by acquiring wealth.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் சுற்றத்தார் தன்னைச் சுற்றி அன்போடு இருக்கும்படி வாழ்வதுதான், அவன் செல்வத்தைப் பெற்றதனால் அடைந்த உண்மையான பயனாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate purpose of acquiring wealth. It states that the true benefit of earning riches is the ability to live surrounded by loving relatives. Wealth is not meant to be hoarded but used to support and embrace one's kin, ensuring they remain close. The word 'சுற்றத்தால்' emphasizes the presence of family, while 'பெற்ற பயன்' highlights that this togetherness is the very fruit of prosperity.

ai.literal: Giving and sweet words if one does, by gathered kin surrounded one will be.
ai.translation: If one can give generously and speak sweet words, one will be surrounded by a growing circle of kin.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் சுற்றத்தாருக்கு வேண்டியதைக் கொடுத்தும், அவர்களிடம் இனிய சொற்களைக் கூறியும் வருவானானால், அவன் பலவாகப் பெருகிய சுற்றத்தால் சூழப்படுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the two essential qualities needed to keep one's relatives close: generosity and pleasant speech. The word 'கொடுத்தல்' refers to sharing one's wealth and resources with kin. The word 'இன்சொல்' emphasizes the importance of speaking to them with kindness and respect. When a person practices both, their extended family will naturally gather around them in ever-increasing numbers, forming a strong support system.

ai.literal: man of great generosity / he harbors not / anger / than him / kin / possessors / in the great world / there are none
ai.translation: In this vast world, no one has more kin than a man of great generosity who harbors no anger.
ai.modern: மிகுந்த கொடைத்தன்மை உடையவனாகவும், சினத்தை மனதில் கொள்ளாதவனாகவும் இருப்பவனை விட, இந்தப் பெரிய உலகத்தில் அதிகமான சுற்றத்தாரை உடையவர் வேறு யாரும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights two essential qualities for gathering and keeping a large circle of family and friends: generosity and a mild temper. 'பெருங்கொடையான்' refers to a person who gives freely and abundantly to others. 'பேணான் வெகுளி' describes someone who does not nurse or hold onto anger. The poet asserts that in the entire world ('மாநிலத்து'), no one will be surrounded by more kin ('மருங்கு உடையார்') than a person who combines these two virtues.

ai.literal: Crow without-concealing having-called eats; wealth-also to-those-of-such-nature-only exist.
ai.translation: The crow does not hide its food, but calls out to its kind and eats with them. Prosperity abides only with people of such a nature.
ai.modern: காக்கை தனக்குக் கிடைத்த உணவை மறைக்காமல் தன் சுற்றத்தைக் கூவி அழைத்துச் சேர்ந்து உண்ணும். செல்வம் அத்தகைய குணம் உடையவர்களிடமே நிலைத்திருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the natural behavior of the crow to illustrate the virtue of sharing with one's kindred. A crow does not hide its food ('கரவா'); instead, it calls out ('கரைந்து') to gather its flock before eating ('உண்ணும்'). The word 'ஆக்கம்' refers to wealth or prosperity, and 'அன்ன நீரார்க்கே' means 'only to those of such nature'. The poem teaches that lasting prosperity belongs only to those who, like the crow, openly share their good fortune with their relatives.

ai.literal: Commonly looking-not, king by merit if looks, that looking at, those who live are many.
ai.translation: If a king does not treat everyone alike but regards each according to their merit, many will live looking up to that discernment.
ai.modern: அரசன் எல்லோரையும் பொதுவாக ஒரே மாதிரியாகப் பார்க்காமல், அவரவர் தகுதிக்கு ஏற்ப மதித்துப் பார்த்தால், அந்தப் பண்பை நம்பி வாழ்பவர்கள் பலராவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how a leader should recognize individual merit. If a king treats everyone exactly the same ('பொது நோக்கான்'), he fails to acknowledge special talents or contributions. Instead, if he looks at people according to their specific rank or merit ('வரிசையா நோக்கின்'), many capable people will be drawn to him and live under his patronage ('அது நோக்கி வாழ்வார் பலர்'). The repetition of the root 'நோக்கு' (look) emphasizes both the leader's discerning vision and the followers' hopeful gaze.

ai.literal: Having been kin those who abandoned oneself kinship estrangement cause without will come.
ai.translation: Relatives who were once close but left you will return when the cause of their estrangement is removed.
ai.modern: முன்பு உறவினராக இருந்து பின் பிரிந்து சென்றவர்களின் உறவு, அவர்கள் பிரிந்ததற்கான காரணம் நீங்கியவுடன் தானாகவே திரும்பி வரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to reunite with estranged relatives. Sometimes family members who were once close leave because of a specific disagreement or displeasure. The poet observes that their kinship is not permanently lost; they will naturally return to the fold once the underlying cause of their estrangement is resolved.

ai.literal: From the side having separated, due to a reason him who came, the king, having examined, having stayed, having considered, should accept.
ai.translation: When an associate who previously left returns for a reason, the king should carefully examine the matter, consider it well, and then accept him back.
ai.modern: தன்னிடம் இருந்து பிரிந்து சென்று, பின் ஒரு காரணத்தால் மீண்டும் தன்னிடம் வந்தவனை, அரசன் அதற்கான காரணத்தை ஆராய்ந்து தீர்த்து, நன்கு சிந்தித்து ஏற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises a leader on how to handle an associate who previously left but has now returned. The word 'உழை' refers to the leader's side or proximity. When such a person returns 'காரணத்தின்' (for a specific reason), the king must not accept them blindly. Instead, he should 'இழைத்து இருந்து எண்ணி'—carefully examine the cause of the separation, resolve any underlying issues, and thoughtfully take them back into his circle.
